_why_locale_is_declared: Every expectation below is the literal text of a node, and Android resolves those strings against the *device's* language, not the listing's. `scripts/media-capture.mjs` compares this value against the device before it takes the capture lock, so a phone in another language is refused in seconds instead of failing every reading in every shot three times over. It was added after exactly that: the slot gained values-<locale>/ directories, the owner's phone is Russian, and shot-01 reported '5 of 5 expected readings are not in the field they name' against a screen that was correct in Russian. The device's own declaration in _preconditions below is prose a human reads; this field is the one a program reads.
_comment: Six-step journey for the Mark Book for Teachers store screenshots, replayed by scripts/media-capture.mjs and framed by scripts/store/render.py. Every coordinate was measured from the live view hierarchy (uiautomator dump) of the signed release build on a physical Samsung Galaxy A40 (R58MB3SGZVL) at 1080x2340 / 480dpi, never guessed.
_why_the_setup_lives_in_shot_01: media-capture runs 'pm clear' before the first shot, so a capture cannot inherit a scene: the record book the screenshots show has to be built by the run itself. A record book is not a form the app can be handed in one screen - a class, a roster, a category, an assignment, six marks, a register and a seating plan are six different surfaces - so the whole scene is built in shot-01's steps and shot-01 is taken once the app is back on the class list. Shots 02-06 are navigation only.
_why_the_average_is_the_check: The six marks are 18, 15, 20, 12, 17 and one missing, so the class average is 410/6 = 68.33%, shown as 68.3%. Round marks (all 10s, or five of six) would let a wrong computation agree with a right one by coincidence; 68.3% can only appear if the category weight, the assignment points and every one of the six cells were read from what was entered. shot-01 asserts it, and it is the single reading that fails if any step of the setup silently did nothing.
_why_one_mark_is_missing: Diego's cell is recorded as missing, not as zero, which is what the reviewed build held: the Grades tab then reads '5 of 6 marked' and '1 missing', and the class list reads 68.3%. It also puts the app's own distinction on screen ('an unmarked cell is not a zero') instead of a screenshot that claims it. The missing state is a first-class choice in the entry dialog (the 'Missing' segment), so it is reproducible: tap the segment instead of typing a score.
_why_the_strip_coordinates_differ_per_sh: SectionStrip scrolls the selected pill into view in the same row it lives in, and only the selected pill draws its label, so it is also the widest pill. The coordinate of a target pill therefore depends on which tab is currently selected, and the four navigation taps below were each measured in the state they are used from: Roster->Grades at (439,374), Grades->Attendance at (619,374), Attendance->Seating at (1023,374). Reports is the exception - reachable only by scrolling the strip to its forward extreme first, because from Seating it sits clipped at the right edge - and at that extreme it was measured at (708,302-852,446), i.e. (780,374).
_why_shot_01_scrolls_to_an_extreme: A fresh class list puts the new class below the fold (measured: after 'Create' the class row is not in the hierarchy at all, and the paywall card is the last thing on screen), so the setup scrolls the list to its bottom extreme with three swipes - extra swipes at an edge are no-ops, which makes the offset a property of the content rather than of a fling's velocity.
_why_shot_06_does_not_scroll: It wants to. The Reports tab puts its four export actions and the backup card below the hero, and the obvious recipe is one more swipe - which is what this journey did first, and the shutter was refused: at the bottom extreme the CSV card's title has scrolled off the top while its description is still on the screen, so 'Spreadsheet (CSV)' is not in the frame and the headline's first claim is not in the picture. Scrolling to a *measured* mid-offset would fix that frame and make it depend on a drag's velocity, which is exactly the instability the extreme recipe exists to avoid. So the shot is taken at the top of the tab, which a fresh composition always starts at, and it asserts the six readings that are on screen there: the hero, both export surfaces this shot photographs, and the backup stat. The backup card itself is a swipe away and is described in store/listing.md instead of being asserted here.
_why_the_expects_are_all_self_identifyin: Every reading below is the text of the node that carries it, anchored with ^...$, because on this app the things worth asserting are computed results and list rows, not values typed into a labelled input: 'Class average: 68.3%', 'Average: 90.0% · 1 attendance mark', '6 of 6 recorded'. Where a labelled field does exist it is asserted as one - the register's date field is labelled 'Register for', the dialogs carry 'Class name', 'Category name', 'Weight (%)', 'Assignment name', 'Points it is worth', 'Rows' and 'Columns', and those are the fields the setup types into, so the typed values land where the label says they are. Every reading is at least two characters, as media-capture refuses shorter ones at load time: a bare '6' or '0' is satisfied by almost any screen.
_why_the_register_is_one_tap: The Attendance tab has a bulk action ('Everyone present', markAllPresent) beside the per-student status chips, and it is above the roster, so its coordinate does not move as the cards below it change height. One tap records all six; the Reading '6 of 6 recorded' and 'Everyone present' are asserted on the frame, so a tap that missed would leave the summary reading '0 of 6 recorded' and fail.
_why_there_is_a_leading_wait: The runner waits one second after launching the app and then executes steps back to back. Compose needs longer than that to draw the class list, and every dialog here is opened, filled and confirmed within a few hundred milliseconds of the tap that opened it. The waits are load-bearing, not padding.
_why_the_clears_are_four_keys_and_not_fo: A 'clear' step is one adb invocation per key press - 123 then N times 67 - so its default of 40 keys is 41 process launches, measured on this device at roughly 1-3 seconds each: a single clear cost about a minute of wall clock, and the first version of this journey had ten of them, which is why one replay of the setup took over twenty minutes instead of five. Four keys are enough for every field it is used on: the two pre-filled 100s, and the seating grid's 5 and 6. The five grade-entry clears were removed outright instead of shortened, because the dialog builds its score field from the cell it edits (ui/components/Average.kt, GradeEntryDialog: 'if (existing?.kind == GradeKind.SCORE) trim(existing.points) else ""') and every cell this journey edits arrives unmarked, so the field is empty and the keys would delete nothing. The three clears that remain are the ones where a default is genuinely present and appending would corrupt the value.
_preconditions: Target the release build. The debug variant carries a .debug applicationId suffix, so capturing it would photograph a package that never ships: node scripts/prepare-release.mjs --slot teacher-gradebook, then adb install -r dist/teacher-gradebook-0.1.0-1-release.apk

A physical device at 1080x2340 / 480dpi with the system language set to English (en-US), because every reading below is English copy. The screens are captured at 1080x2340, so the phone assets are framed from a 2340px-tall source rather than 1920.
The device must not be asleep: a locked screen silently swallows the taps and the first shot then fails with an empty hierarchy. Wake it and dismiss the keyguard before the run.

The app must be a first run: media-capture enforces this itself with 'pm clear', so the empty state the setup builds on cannot be inherited from an earlier run, and it retries 'ime disable' until the enabled list is empty because a live keyboard autocorrects typed values and rescrolls the form.

No purchase is made by this journey. The free tier holds one class and twenty students, so the setup fits inside it, and the Reports frame deliberately shows the free tier's own state ('unlock to export or back them up') rather than a screen a free user cannot reach.

The tablet assets are composed from these same phone captures rather than captured on a tablet device, because no tablet device is attached; Play treats large-screen assets as a claim about the large-screen experience, so this phone-framed status is disclosed in store/review-notes.md and store/README.md instead of being passed off as a tablet capture.
